news.headline: A Space Telescope Spots a Giant Cat's Head in the Stars
news.body: Meow! NASA's James Webb Space Telescope took a new picture of a huge cloud of gas and dust shaped like a cat's head. It's called the Cat's Head Nebula, and it sits inside a bigger cloud named the Carina Nebula. Super-bright stars nearby blow strong winds and blast powerful light that wear away the softer parts of the cloud, kind of like waves shaping sand. The thicker parts stay behind, leaving a pointy-eared kitty in space!

news.headline: A Teeny Baby Deer Is Born at a Zoo in Japan
news.body: A zoo in Kobe, Japan, has a brand-new pudu fawn! Pudus are the smallest deer in the whole world, and they come from South America. The little boy fawn was named Sazanka, after a pretty winter flower. When he was born in early October, he weighed only about 1.6 pounds, less than a big bag of apples. In just a few weeks, he doubled his weight! His white baby spots will fade away in two or three months.

news.headline: A 13-Year-Old Builds a Solar Gadget to Skip a Chore
news.body: Jason Chang, a seventh grader in Massachusetts, kept getting sent outside to tilt the solar panels on holiday lights so they faced the sun. So he invented a tracker that turns a solar panel all by itself, using gravity instead of electricity! It cost less than $25 to build. In tests, his moving panel made about 20 percent more power than a panel that stayed still. Now he's a national STEM champion!
